$provenance.derivation: Hand-authored per D21. The top-level KEY SET was confirmed key-by-key against the ORDERS_PAID sample in the webhook reference (93 top-level keys; every key listed in documented_keys below was individually confirmed present). Values are invented. No live capture; no Shopify credential exists here (D3).
caveats: This recording's `payload` carries a SUBSET of the real sample's top-level keys — the ones this system reads. `documented_keys[""]` lists 57 real key names, which is NOT the sample's full top-level key count; the earlier wording here claimed it was the "full confirmed set", and that was false and flattering, because it made a partial enumeration read as complete coverage of the invented-key check. Every name listed was individually confirmed present in the sample; names absent from the list are not thereby claimed to be absent from Shopify.

`customer` is present in the real payload as a full object with email, phone, first_name, last_name and default_address. It is null here and in the stub BY DESIGN: SPEC C5 says the app holds no protected-customer-data scopes. This is a deliberate divergence, not a transcription gap.

`note_attributes` IS present on the orders/paid sample, but its value there is `[]`, so the {name, value} element shape below comes from the REST Order resource page rather than from the webhook sample.

`fulfillments` is likewise [] in every webhook sample. The seven-key element shape below is the abbreviated form printed on the REST Order page. Whether a real webhook embeds that or the larger standalone Fulfillment shape is NOT documented.

CORRECTION (this header previously described the evidence backwards). It claimed only "fixed_amount" appears in the published examples. On the webhooks page the truth is the reverse: `fixed_amount` appears ZERO times anywhere on it, and '"value_type": "percentage"' appears twice — though both are in draft-order payloads, not in an order one. So the page supports `percentage` as a real value_type while confirming nothing about which value_type an ORDER carries. The stub emits `percentage` for a percentage discount; treat that as reasoned, not cited.
`checkout_id` does NOT appear anywhere in the webhook reference (0 occurrences) even though it is a real REST Order field. It is deliberately absent here.

IMPORTANT, and missed on the first pass: `discount_applications` and `discount_codes` are BOTH `[]` in the orders/paid sample — as they are in every orders/* sample on that page. So neither element shape below is transcribed from that sample; both come from the REST Order resource page. This matters because those two arrays are the entire discount surface this system reads, and the page cited as `source` shows them empty.

The sample has exactly 93 top-level keys (extracted and JSON-parsed twice, from the rendered HTML and from the canonical markdown, with identical results). Every one of the 57 names in documented_keys[""] was checked to be a member of that set, and every key this stub emits is a member of it too.

headers.X-Shopify-Hmac-Sha256: <base64 HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body, keyed by the app client secret>

header_notes: shopify.dev prints the HMAC header three ways across its own pages (X-Shopify-Hmac-Sha256, X-Shopify-Hmac-SHA256, x-shopify-hmac-sha256) and states that header names must be treated as case-insensitive. X-Shopify-Name is also real but optional and is not sent by the stub.

payload.$may_be_empty_note: Every OTHER array recorded here must arrive populated: an empty `line_items` or `note_attributes` on an orders/paid body is a defect, and the shape check now reports it. These two are the exceptions -- they are empty for an undiscounted order, and the published sample they were derived from has BOTH `[]`. Marking them here is what keeps the non-empty rule from false-positiving on a legitimate no-discount order.
